scenes.title: Eight Hours on the Clock
scenes.summary: At eight Thursday morning, F1, M2, and M4 coordinate the final eight-hour checklist before the National Guidebook Editor and photographer arrive at four sharp.
scenes.intro: Brilliant Thursday morning sunshine pours into the lobby of {SHOW} at eight sharp. {F1} holds a crisp clipboard while {M2} checks his pocket watch and {M4} rolls up his sleeves before work. Listen first.
story: M2
Eight hours until the National Guidebook camera tripod crosses our stone threshold, team!
F1
Item One: {M3} and {M4} hang all six Boston ferns along the iron tie-beams.
M4
My brother already tested the six ceiling hooks with sandbags—each holds thirty kilos!
F1
Item Two: {M1} heats the soapstone thermal bricks to test the eighteen-ninety bread warmer.
M2
And Item Three: {F2} bakes twelve medallion-stamped saffron-cardamom loaves by three-fifteen!
M4
Did Number Twelve confirm she will open her eastern oak door for the wide shot?
F1
Better yet, she swept her entire garden courtyard and set out potted camellias!
M2
Meanwhile I shall personally polish the brass wall plaques inside the conservatory until noon!
F1
Remember {M1} and his strict warning last night, {M2}: polish brass, NEVER turn wheels!
M2
Please, {F1}, I can distinguish an ornamental brass rosette from a water valve!
M4
Only when your reading glasses stay down below your eyebrows, {M2}!
F1
Stations, everyone—let us make eighteen-ninety shine before four this afternoon!
scenes.outro: Every task has a captain—provided {M2} keeps his glasses low around century-old brass plumbing! See you inside the vault next time.

scenes.title: Soapstone Thermal Bricks
scenes.summary: At ten-thirty inside the conservatory, M1 slides oven-warmed soapstone bricks into the lower drawer of the 1890 ceramic alcove, filling the bread cabinet with gentle dry heat.
scenes.intro: Wearing heavy leather work mitts inside the sunlit conservatory, {M1} slides four clean grey soapstone blocks into the lower iron drawer beneath the cobalt bread-warming chamber as {F2} and {F3} watch closely. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
Amazing—not a single flame or ember inside the conservatory, yet feel that warmth!
M1
Dense grey soapstone holds kitchen-oven heat for five straight hours without scorching a crust.
F3
Hold your palm near the upper porcelain shelf, {F2}—it feels like a summer bakery!
F2
Forty degrees of gentle radiant warmth, so braided loaves stay pillow-soft until six tonight!
M1
And zero smoke or soot ever touches the glazed blue bricks or the ferns.
F3
Nineteenth-century engineers solved sustainable catering a century before anyone invented electric warming trays!
F2
Wait until I slide twelve saffron-glazed wheat-and-lyre loaves onto these two shelves at three!
M1
Close the pierced brass lattice doors now so the ceramic chamber preheats evenly.
F3
Listen—who is whistling merrily down at the far north corner with a rag?
M1
Uh-oh... {M2} found that brass pipe wheel beneath the overhead fern mister.
F2
{M1}, walk down there fast—his reading glasses just rode up onto his forehead!
M1
BOSS, DO NOT TWIST THAT BRASS PIPE WHEEL COUNTERCLOCKWISE RIGHT NOW!
scenes.outro: Radiant soapstone heat works like a dream—one second before {M2} twists a mysterious 1890 brass wheel! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Eighteen-Ninety Fern Mister
scenes.summary: Twisting a tarnished brass wheel while buffing it without his glasses, M2 activates the 1890 overhead rainwater fern mister straight onto his own shoulders before M1 shuts the stopcock.
scenes.intro: At the northern corner of the glass gallery, {M2} gives a small brass wall wheel one brisk turn with his polishing cloth—and freezes as a fine tropical mist showers gently from three overhead brass roses directly onto his jacket! {M1} strides up calmly. Listen first.
story: M2
{M1}! WHY IS THE CONSERVATORY CEILING RAINING INDOORS UNDER A CLEAR BLUE SKY?!
M1
Because you just opened the eighteen-ninety gravity fern-mister connected to our roof cistern.
M2
Turn it off! Turn it off before my best Thursday tweed jacket shrinks two sizes!
M1
Clockwise half a turn... hiss... and dry again inside three seconds flat.
M2
I thought that brass wheel was merely a decorative Victorian coat hook, {M1}!
M1
Coat hooks rarely have copper water pipes soldered into both ends, boss.
M2
Well... look on the bright side: those nineteenth-century brass mist nozzles still work magnificently!
M1
True enough—not a single clogged pinhole after sixty dry years, and zero leaks.
M2
Did any spray reach our warm bread cabinet or the dry table linen?
M1
Only your shoulders and your pride; everything south of rib two stayed bone dry.
M2
Thank heavens I pressed my spare navy-blue blazer upstairs this morning!
M1
Go change into dry wool while {M3} and {M4} hang the six ferns underneath.
scenes.outro: {M2} accidentally proves the 1890 plant-misting plumbing still works—at the modest cost of one damp tweed jacket! See you next time.

scenes.title: Hanging the Six Boston Ferns
scenes.summary: At one-thirty inside the sparkling conservatory, M3, M4, and F1 suspend six lush green Boston ferns along the overhead iron tie-beams.
scenes.intro: Sunlight sparkles off wet leaves at the north end as {M3} and {M4} steady a tall wooden stepladder, lifting lush green Boston ferns sent by Number Twelve onto the wrought-iron tie-beams while {F1} checks sightlines below. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M4
Hook number five engaged on the brass swivel—how does the height look, {F1}?
F1
Perfection! High enough for tall guests, yet framing the arched skylight in emerald green!
M3
Clap your hands once at the centre line, {F1}, now that all six ferns hang.
F1
Clap! Oh, listen—that tiny glass flutter overhead softened into velvet warmth!
M4
Sixteen-inch fern fronds work better than any modern foam ceiling baffle in town!
M3
And next week {M1} can actually mist all six ferns together in three seconds!
F1
Provided nobody stands underneath wearing tweed when {M1} turns that brass wheel!
M4
Ready to carry in the long walnut table so it straddles the mosaic line?
F1
Lift together on three: two legs in Plot Fourteen-A, two legs in Plot Fourteen-B!
M3
Matched to the nineteen-oh-five sepia postcard right down to the bevelled glass doors behind!
M4
Here comes {M2} looking remarkably crisp in his dry navy blazer—with one pair of glasses!
F1
Time to lay twenty-four alternating cobalt and cream teacups down the centre!
scenes.outro: Six emerald ferns crown the iron vault while one shared walnut table bridges two historic plots once again! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Spare Navy Blazer
scenes.summary: At half past two, F1 and F3 help M2 arrange the alternating cobalt-and-cream table settings and rehearse a concise, authentic historical welcome.
scenes.intro: Stepping between the sunny courtyard and the open 1890 oak arch at half past two, {M2} smooths his crisp dry navy blazer while {F1} and {F3} arrange porcelain cups along the shared walnut table. Let us listen in first.
story: F3
Navy wool suits you splendidly, {M2}—and look at blue and cream porcelain alternating!
M2
Twelve cobalt star cups from Number Twelve beside twelve cream stoneware cups from {SHOW}!
F1
When the Chief Editor asks how two neighbours reopened a sixty-year arch, what do we say?
M2
No grand speeches: we found six saved blue tiles, apologized honestly, and turned two keys.
F3
Keep every single word of that answer, {M2}—editors recognize genuine truth immediately.
F1
And our Room Five postmaster lent his eighteen-ninety-two copperplate postal survey for the side easel!
M2
Plus our neighbour at Number Twelve set three hand-painted amphora vases along the eastern bench!
F3
My violin partner from Number Ten arrives at half past three for soft background chamber music.
F1
Which leaves forty-five minutes for {F2} and {M4} to pull twelve golden loaves out!
M2
Smell that saffron, honey, and toasted sesame drifting across the courtyard already!
F3
Keep your hands safely in your blazer pockets near brass valves until four, {M2}.
M2
Hands folded behind my back like a museum curator until the camera clicks!
scenes.outro: Alternating blue and cream porcelain tells a sixty-year peace story without a single chalk line in sight! See you in the kitchen next time.

scenes.title: Golden Loaves Stamped with Lyres
scenes.summary: At three-twenty in the café kitchen, F2, M4, and F1 draw twelve gleaming saffron-honey loaves from the ovens and carry them out to the heated 1890 ceramic alcove.
scenes.intro: Twenty past three in the warm café kitchen! {F2} opens both oven doors, releasing a golden cloud of cardamom, saffron, and roasted sesame as {M4} and {F1} stand ready with linen-draped boards. Listen first.
story: M4
Look at those twelve round crowns—every single wheat sheaf and lyre stamped crystal clear!
F2
Six stamped with the musical lyre, six stamped with the ceramic amphora and wheat!
F1
Brush the last drop of wildflower honey across loaf twelve while the crust sings, {F2}!
F2
Listen to that tiny crackle along the golden glaze—light inside and crisp outside!
M4
Ten loaves slide straight onto the warm soapstone shelves inside the eighteen-ninety alcove.
F1
And two uncut centrepiece loaves sit on wooden boards right across the mosaic boundary line!
F2
Did {M1} check the temperature inside the cobalt warming chamber five minutes ago?
M4
Steady at thirty-eight degrees—warm enough to perfume both courtyards the moment doors open!
F1
Carry board number one steadily, {M4}; it is twenty-five minutes to four!
F2
Four pots of fresh mint and jasmine tea steep at five minutes to four sharp.
F1
From an ivy-covered mystery on Saturday night to a living eighteen-ninety bakery on Thursday!
F2
Out to the glass vault—let us set the warm shelves before the taxi arrives!
scenes.outro: Twelve golden medallion loaves perfume the conservatory air with twenty minutes left on the clock! See you under the glass vault next time.

scenes.title: Both Oak Doors Wide Open
scenes.summary: At ten to four inside the sunlit conservatory, F2 slides the stamped loaves behind the brass lattice while F3 and M3 check the serene acoustic balance.
scenes.intro: At three-fifty, golden late-afternoon sunshine slants at forty-five degrees through a hundred spotless glass panes, turning every gold-starred cobalt brick radiant as {F2}, {F3}, and {M3} take a quiet breath inside the gallery. Listen first.
story: F2
Ten warm loaves glowing behind pierced brass lattice, and two centrepieces on the walnut table!
M3
Look straight west into our courtyard tree, then straight east into those bright camellias!
F3
With the bevelled glass wind-doors closed gently in the middle, zero breeze disturbs the ferns.
M3
Play one quiet pizzicato chord with Number Ten beside the alcove, {F3}, and test it.
F3
Soft, round, and clear—whisper a secret here and someone smiles across the room!
F2
Look through the eastern arch: our neighbour wore a cobalt silk scarf matching her cups!
M3
And did she set that restored six-tile sign on a cedar easel beside the doorway?!
F3
Two courtyards separated for sixty years looking as though they never missed a single afternoon.
F2
Hear the front gate bell ringing out on {STREET} right on the dot of four?!
M3
That is {F1} and {M2} welcoming the National Guidebook Editor and photographer right now!
F3
Bow poised, {M3}; let them hear music floating out before they turn the corner.
F2
Welcome back to the golden sunlight of eighteen-ninety, {CITY}!
scenes.outro: Sunlight, cobalt glaze, warm cardamom bread, and gentle strings unite both courtyards right on the stroke of four! Final scene of Episode 5!

scenes.title: Camera Cases at the Gate
scenes.summary: At four sharp at the front gate, M2 lifts the iron latch smoothly on the first try as F1, M2, and M1 welcome the National Guidebook Editor and photographer toward the glowing 1890 arch.
scenes.intro: Four chimes ring across {STREET} as a town taxi halts outside {SHOW}. Carrying leather camera cases, two eager visitors approach the stone entrance while {F1}, {M2}, and {M1} step forward beneath the cream-and-gold pennants. Listen first.
story: M1
Remember the rule, boss: lift slightly first, one pair of glasses, zero plumbing valves.
M2
Calm as a summer lake, {M1}—lifting latch smoothly... open on the first try!
F1
Good afternoon, Chief Editor, and welcome back to {SHOW} on {STREET}!
M2
Right past our founding eighteen-ninety oval plaque and our new Golden Courtyard Plaque!
F1
Wait—look at the photographer stopping dead in his tracks halfway across our flagstones!
M1
Where rosemary stood on Saturday, he now sees twelve metres of glass and blue brick.
M2
Did you hear the editor gasp?! She thought the eighteen-ninety arch was bricked solid forever!
F1
Wait until she steps inside and sees BOTH historic courtyards open end to end!
M1
The photographer is already reaching for his widest portrait lens before setting down his bag.
M2
Invite them straight across the threshold, {F1}—and wave our neighbour in from Plot Fourteen-B!
F1
Step right through the eighteen-ninety oak doorway—warm tea and history are waiting!
M1
Not bad for five days of honest work behind an ivy bush.
scenes.outro: Where thick ivy stood five nights ago, a sunlit 1890 glass gallery leaves the National Guidebook team speechless! End of Episode 5—see you in the Season 5 finale!
